Reddit Sinks 8% as Social Ad Worries Deepen in Tech Rout ©Brett Jordan from Pexels via Canva and sasirin pamai's Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

Reddit shares fell 8% today after Snap reported just 4% ad revenue growth, in a broad tech selloff.

Meta's 26% revenue growth last quarter suggests advertisers are still spending on the biggest social platform, so Snap's slowdown looks like Snap's own problem.

Reddit's bigger risk is the search traffic it's losing to AI answers on Alphabet's Google, which is why its fourth-quarter guidance disappointed.

The next big test for Reddit is its data-licensing renewal with Google, due in early 2027.

Reddit (RDDT:NYSE) sank 8% today. A weak quarter from Snap and a broad tech rout hit a stock that was already reeling from its own disappointing outlook.

Snap's ad revenue grew just 4% in the third quarter, and CEO Evan Spiegel said on its call that "advertising revenue growth remains below our ambitions." That's an ugly line for any ad-funded social app. But Meta Platforms (META:NASDAQ), the biggest of them, is telling a different story. And Reddit's real headache is still the traffic it's losing to Alphabet (GOOGL:NASDAQ).

Snap's problem looks like Snap's

Snap tied a drop in brand advertising to consumer packaged goods companies spending less. Meta isn't seeing that. Its third-quarter revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion, and it guided to $73 billion to $76 billion of fourth-quarter revenue. Meta shares are down 4% today, less than QQQ's 6% drop.

Reddit's own sales haven't cracked either: revenue rose 53% to $895 million in the third quarter.

The bigger worry is Google

Last week, Reddit said its search referral traffic fell meaningfully in the third quarter. It also guided fourth-quarter revenue to $1.00 billion to $1.03 billion, short of what analysts expected. CEO Steve Huffman blamed AI Overviews and AI Mode in Google Search.

Those searches haven't gone away. Alphabet's third-quarter Search & other revenue rose 12% to $63.4 billion, and CEO Sundar Pichai said Google's query growth was "the highest it's been in the last five years." Alphabet shares are down 2% today.

Analysts still expect Reddit's revenue to keep climbing fast through 2028.

Reddit (RDDT): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2024-2028 (TIKR)

I don't see Snap's quarter changing those estimates much, because Reddit's own fourth-quarter guidance still implies growth of roughly 38% to 42%. Google could change them. Analysts have already trimmed their 2027 revenue estimate to $4.34 billion, from $4.47 billion in late October.

Key Takeaways

Pinterest shares fell 7% today, along with Reddit, after Snap reported 4% ad growth during a broad tech selloff.

Snap's sluggish ad sales echo Pinterest's report last week, when ad prices fell 4% and its fourth-quarter guide missed estimates.

Meta grew revenue 26% and Reddit 53%, so the ad slowdown looks specific to Pinterest and Snap.

Pinterest trades far below its usual forward P/E, but until its ad prices turn back up, the discount looks deserved.

Pinterest (PINS:NYSE) stock is down 7% today after Snap said its third-quarter ad revenue grew just 4%.

The selling is broad: Reddit (RDDT:NYSE) is off 9%, and Meta Platforms (META:NASDAQ) is down 4%. But Snap's quarter reads a lot like Pinterest's own.

Snap's quarter sounds familiar

Snap's revenue rose 14% to $1.72 billion, but advertising grew only 4%.

Pinterest's Oct. 29 report looked similar. Revenue rose 12% to $1.17 billion, and ad prices fell 4%. Its fourth-quarter guide of $1.425 billion-$1.475 billion came in below the roughly $1.52 billion analysts expected.

Meta keeps raising its prices

Meta's third-quarter revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion, and its average price per ad rose 14%. My read: ad budgets are pooling at the biggest platform.

Reddit is the exception among the smaller players: its third-quarter revenue rose 53% to $895 million. But its daily active uniques held at 130.3 million from the second quarter, and its fourth-quarter guide fell short of Wall Street's estimates. Its next report will show whether flat users start to slow its ad growth.

Analysts already expect slower growth

Analysts see Pinterest's revenue growth slowing from 16% in 2025 to about 12% a year in 2027 and 2028:

Pinterest (PINS): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2023-2028 (TIKR)

They trimmed their 2027 estimate to $5.41 billion from $5.55 billion after last week's report. Nothing in Snap's report is about Pinterest's own business, so I wouldn't expect another round of cuts from it.

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Pinterest, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Pinterest's Analyst Ratings

Cheap for a reason

Pinterest traded at 9.2x forward earnings at the last close, against a five-year average of 23.7x:

Pinterest (PINS): forward (NTM) P/E, last 5 years (TIKR)

At today's price, it's even lower. But stock pay of $288 million took nearly all of the third quarter's $300 million of free cash flow, so the discount isn't as deep as it looks.

The way I see it, today's drop is mostly the market, but investors are right to link Pinterest to Snap. Until Pinterest's ad prices turn back up, I'd expect the stock to trade like a company losing ground to Meta. Its fourth-quarter report in early February, with its first 2027 outlook, is the next chance to change that.

A user miss and slow advertising growth are overshadowing the return to profitability at Snap (NYSE:SNAP). Snap stock is at $5.30 in morning trading, down 11%. The Snapchat parent swung to a profit in Q3 2026, though its daily active users fell short of estimates and subscriptions supplied more of the growth than ads did.

stockcam / Getty Images

Adding to the pressure, Snap is changing how it measures its audience, switching daily active users for monthly active users as its headline metric. Combined with ad growth that management admits is falling short of its goals, the change is giving traders reason to question how durable the turnaround at Snap is.

Snap Swings to a Profit as Users Fall Short

Snap Inc. disclosed on November 4, after the close, that its Q3 revenue rose 14% year over year (YoY) to $1.72 billion. The result came in slightly short of the $1.73 billion consensus estimate, missing expectations. Snap Inc. reported Snapchat daily active users of 495 million, below the 499 million Stocktwits estimate.

Profitability told a better story for the company. Net income at Snap reached $56 million, compared with a $104 million net loss a year earlier. Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) at Snap Inc. rose to $383 million.

Guidance from Snap calls for Q4 2026 revenue of $1.95 billion to $1.99 billion, a range that starts at the $1.95 billion consensus. Management also guided adjusted EBITDA to $490 million to $525 million.

Reddit (RDDT) stock fell 41.4% between May 7 and November 3, 2026, while the S&P 500 returned 3.7% over the same dates. The stock suffered its largest one-day drop of that stretch on October 30. That decline came the day after Reddit reported its third quarter and said its daily users could fall in the fourth. So how big is that warning about daily users against the business Reddit runs today?

Reddit Warned That Its Daily Users Could Fall

The warning applies first to the user count, and less directly to revenue. During an October 29 call, management said daily users could fall by a low double-digit percentage in the fourth quarter from a current base of 130 million, if an October drop in visitors from search continues. Yet logged-in users generate over 80% of Reddit's revenue, management said on the same call, adding that engagement from its app and logged-in users is still growing. A still significant number of users arriving from search land on the mobile website instead of the app, management also said.

Most of the six-month decline occurred late in the period. Reddit stock fell 29.2% on October 30 alone, and it lost 36.1% between October 5 and November 3, a period when the S&P 500 lost 2.6%.

Holders face a second risk. During the fourth quarter, Reddit will begin testing a logged-in-only version of the site in select markets outside the U.S., and management expects to trade some reach for engagement.

How Fast Does Reddit Now Expect Sales To Grow?

Management said on the call that Reddit expects fourth-quarter revenue of $1 billion to $1.03 billion, up 38% to 42% from a year earlier. That pace trails the 53% growth Reddit reported for the third quarter. Revenue growth had already eased in each quarter of 2026, slowing from 69.1% in the first.

The decline has made Reddit's profits much cheaper to buy. At the November 3 close, the stock traded at 18.7 times its last twelve months of earnings, against 22.8 for the S&P 500. At the end of September, that multiple stood at 27.7.

Reddit Still Earns Far More Than A Year Ago

Reddit's latest financial figures run through September, capturing the period before most of the stock's decline. The company posted an operating margin of 29.4% over the twelve months to September 30, 2026, compared with 13.8% over the twelve months before. Over the same twelve months, Reddit produced $1.2 billion of free cash flow.

Reddit also carries almost no debt, ending September with $3.03 billion in cash and short-term investments against about $31 million of debt. So far the warning is about users, while Reddit's margin and cash stand where its last report placed them. The number to watch is Reddit's daily user count, the figure management warned about, when the company reports its fourth quarter, expected in February 2027.

Reddit Investment Narrative Recap

To own Reddit, you need to believe the logged in community and its ad and data monetization can stay healthy even if headline traffic softens. The key short term swing factor is whether the planned logged in only experience and weaker Google referrals translate into the guided low double digit DAU decline or something more contained.

The biggest risk right now sits squarely in user durability and advertiser confidence if DAUs keep slipping after Q4. Q3 numbers and guidance show the core business still producing revenue and profit, so the story has shifted from financials to execution on engagement and product design around that smaller, more monetized audience.

The completed US$340.37 million buyback, covering 1.15% of shares, lands right as the stock has fallen sharply on DAU and referral worries. That repurchase does not change the operating issues, but it slightly tightens the share count while the market is repricing the risk around user trends.

Viewed against Reddit's recent inclusion in the S&P 500 and its current profitability, this capital return provides a financial cushion around a story now dominated by traffic pressure and the logged in pivot. The core focus is whether Reddit can stabilise usage while keeping ad demand and data licensing on track through that transition.

Reddit's current analyst narrative points to forecast revenue of US$6.1b and projected earnings of US$2.1b by 2029, based on an assumed 25.1% yearly revenue growth rate and an earnings increase of roughly US$1.1b from US$991.7m today.

Reddit (RDDT) stock fell 29.2% on October 30, 2026, during the first trading session after its fiscal Q3 2026 report. The S&P 500 lost 1.8% on the same day. This marks a steep fall following a quarter where revenue of $895 million came in about 2% above what analysts had expected. So what did Reddit tell investors that its results did not?

Reddit Warned Of A Drop In Daily Users

During the October 29 call, management said daily users could fall by a low double-digit percentage in the fourth quarter from a current base of 130 million. The warning came from search. Traffic that search engines send to Reddit fell meaningfully in fiscal Q3 2026, and the decline sped up late in the quarter. In October, those referrals dropped by more than 1 million a week on average, and management's estimate for users assumes that pace continues.

The results themselves held no surprise of that size. Earnings per share came in at $1.40, above the $1.33 analysts expected. Reddit's peers fell far less on the same day. Meta Platforms fell 1.5% and Alphabet fell 1.4%, while Pinterest, the weakest of the three peers, fell 2.8%. The fall was Reddit's own, not its industry's.

Is Reddit's Slowdown More Than One Quarter?

It is for sales growth. Reddit's revenue grew 69.1% from a year earlier in fiscal Q1 2026, a shade below the 69.7% posted in fiscal Q4 2025. Growth then slowed to 61.1% in fiscal Q2 2026 and to 53.0% in fiscal Q3 2026. Management expects growth to slow again in fiscal Q4 2026, forecasting revenue of $1 billion to $1.03 billion, or 38% to 42% growth. News reports on October 30 said that outlook was lower than expected. The traffic warning is new, but the slower growth is not.

Profitability is another matter. Reddit reported an operating margin of 29.2% in fiscal Q3 2026, compared with 23.7% a year earlier.

Management argued that Reddit is still growing where it counts: engagement from its app and logged-in users. About 80% of Reddit's monetization happens within that group, management said. The company added that Reddit is still a top search term in Google, and that Google is simply not sending people to Reddit the way it used to.

When Will Reddit's User Count Be Known?

The fiscal Q4 2026 results will be Reddit's first report since the warning. During that quarter, management plans to begin fully testing a logged-in-only version of Reddit in select markets outside the U.S. The company said the change would likely trade reach for engagement, noting that it will keep evaluating how it reports users.
